record_identity.title: AI-generated professional impersonation used to induce financial payment and identity-document disclosure

summary: AI Incident Database incident 1660 reports that scammers used purportedly AI-generated videos impersonating Miami immigration attorney Angel Leal to solicit a Bronx legal resident seeking U.S. citizenship, resulting in a reported $4,820 payment and disclosure of Social Security and residency documents. The incident is preserved as an identity, representation and deception signal. The available registry evidence identifies the affected technology only at the class level—synthetic video generation, synthetic media generation, deepfake technology and social-media distribution—and does not identify a specific model or provider.
why_it_matters_to_CAM: The incident combines synthetic identity representation, professional-authority impersonation, financial inducement and sensitive identity-document capture. It is relevant to VIGIL's identity, provenance, deceptive-behaviour and authority boundaries, but the current intake did not identify a single existing FM whose threshold can be confidently applied without a broader reconciliation. Preserving the incident now avoids losing the evidence while keeping classification bounded by what is actually known.
evidence_confidence: incident-registry evidence; underlying impersonation and loss are reported allegations and the generating technology/provider is not identified
